question: What IP rating does the idOil Solar enclosure have?
expected_answer: The manual contradicts itself: p. 8 says a lockable IP65 polycarbonate housing, but the technical specifications on p. 54 say IP43 with two ventilation devices. The beacon is IP67 (p. 11), which is a distractor. [All source pages: 8, 11, 54.] [Scoring: Correct if it notes the conflict or gives IP43 from the specs; partly correct if it gives IP65 only; wrong if it gives IP67.]
answer: The idOil Solar Control unit has a lockable IP65 polycarbonate housing [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 8]. The idOil Solar alarm unit has an IP rating of IP43 with two ventilation devices [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 54]. The beacon is IP67 rated [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 11].

question: How long does the idOil Solar keep working without sunlight, and how long can the beacon flash during an alarm?
expected_answer: At least 6 months without sunlight; with the beacon flashing in an alarm about 10 days without sunlight. Battery life is normally about 5 years. [All source pages: 9, 11.] [Scoring: Two facts from two sections; partly correct if only one.]
answer: The idOil Solar will function for at least 6 months without any sunlight [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 9]. In case of an alarm, the idOil Solar can operate the flashing beacon for about 10 days with no sun-light, before the battery becomes discharged [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 11].

question: How do I log in to the idOil Solar browser interface for the first time?
expected_answer: Press the reset button briefly (twice if the device is already on) to switch on the WLAN; connect to the device WLAN with the password = five zeros + the last eight characters of the serial number (e.g. 000001112118J); open 192.168.0.1 in the browser. question: The idOil Solar display backlight is flashing and a fault alarm is on. What should the technician check?
expected_answer: Cause: the sensor cable is short-circuited, cut or disconnected, or the sensor is damaged. Measure the voltage at that sensor's connectors (9.0-11.5 V); if correct, measure the sensor current (should settle at 6.0-8.0 mA within 10 s); reconnect the wire afterwards. [All source pages: 53.]
answer: If the idOil device's display backlight is flashing, the technician can deactivate this function to save power [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 43]. Additionally, the technician should check the battery voltage level, as the idOil device has a setting for a battery low voltage alarm [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 43].

question: How can the measurement interval of the idOil Solar be changed by SMS, which values are allowed, and what is the default?
expected_answer: Command MI <minutes>. Allowed values 10, 30, 60, 120, 180, 240, 360, 480, 600, 720, 1440. Factory default 10 min. Only for 3G versions. [All source pages: 48, 42, 55.] [Scoring: Partly correct if the value list is incomplete.]
answer: The measurement interval (MI) can be set using the command format: MI <nnnn> [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 48]. The permitted values for the measurement interval in minutes are: 10, 30, 60, 120, 180, 240, 360, 480, 600, 720, 1440 [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 48]. The factory default for the measurement intervals is 10 minutes [DOC1599_idOil-Solar-User-Manual-EN.pdf, p. 48].
